decisions.reason: Huineng's three-part formula makes formlessness the basis beside non-thought and non-abiding; later teachers raise the triad publicly and ask which line carries life and death.
A live saying can turn without colliding with the named taboo; teachers contrast that responsive freedom with a dead saying and test whether death itself can open into life.
Following scent and chasing breath names derivative pursuit of verbal traces; masters use the tracking image to expose people running after cases while missing what stands underfoot.

Ten of eleven exact hits are accidental segmentation or ordinary contrast; the old-case reading occurs only as a suffix in one work, so the string does not clear the lexical-unit and independent-deployment gates.

decisions.target: the Four Hoaryheads of Mount Shang
decisions.reason: The Four Hoaryheads of Mount Shang are the recluses invoked in verses and public answers as a compact image of withdrawal, height, and the four appearing as one.
Dead-tree teaching names still, lifeless quietism; masters invoke Shishuang's withered-tree line and then attack fixation on that condition as a difficult dead-water disease.
The late teacher's final saying is a predecessor's deathbed line preserved, requested, or pointed out by heirs; its force comes from named transmission at the edge of death.

decisions.target: trying to fill a net by blowing into it
decisions.reason: Trying to fill a net by blowing into it is the corpus's image for an impossible effort, especially trying to obtain life-and-death understanding by collecting or inflating words.
Bian He's three presentations recall the loyal offer of jade that cost him both feet; Chan verses turn the allusion into a measure of presenting what is precious despite repeated rejection.

decisions.target: whatever meets the eye is the Way
decisions.reason: Whatever meets the eye is the Way is not left as a slogan: teachers remove the sauce jar, demand what then is the Way, and use the formula to test unselective seeing.

Without resting or stopping is Yunfeng's counter-formula to Shishuang's rest-and-cease language, sending activity through crowded streets, thorns, blades, and fire instead of settling in cold stillness.

Southern suddenness and northern gradualness names the historical contrast drawn between Huineng's southern teaching and Shenxiu's northern instruction while explicitly denying that the lineage itself has two geographic essences.
Originally unmoving belongs to Huineng's awakening declaration about self-nature; later teachers quote it and turn it back into a question against claims that mind moves.
Annihilationist emptiness is the condemned blank that erases causation, moral difference, or responsive functioning; the records distinguish it from emptiness that does not destroy consequences.

Ignorance itself is great wisdom is repeatedly quoted as a dangerous slogan when used to excuse conduct; masters preserve the equation while attacking the inference that restraint and consequences therefore vanish.

decisions.target: seeing may be slow or swift
decisions.reason: Seeing may be slow or swift is Huineng's distinction: the teaching is not divided, but people differ in how quickly they see, a line transmitted in several independent records.
Gradual cultivation and sudden awakening names one ordered relation in the fourfold gradual/sudden taxonomy; Chan texts also test whether either ordering substitutes for personally arriving.
A question presenting one's understanding is a public-interview category in which the questioner displays an attained formulation for the teacher to inspect, answer, or overturn.
Clean and utterly bare describes having shed every attachment until nothing can be grasped; funeral and assembly uses retain the stripped, exposed image rather than a cleanliness ritual.
Doushuai's three barriers are the named sequence asking where one's nature is, how one escapes birth and death after seeing it, and where one goes when the elements disperse.

decisions.target: scold the Buddha and berate the patriarchs
decisions.reason: To scold the Buddha and berate the patriarchs is a boast of uncompromising Chan speech, but Yangqi immediately warns that the line must not be raised wrongly before clear-eyed people.

decisions.target: the case of the mud ox entering the sea
decisions.reason: The case of the mud ox entering the sea is a named raised case whose thunderous presentation precipitates a recorded breakthrough; the title identifies the case, not every free occurrence of the image.
Beans bursting in cold ashes images sudden living response where only spent coldness seemed to remain; verses pair the burst with iron trees flowering and an encounter's startling word.
Observe mind as no-mind directs attention to mind without establishing a mind-object; one exposition quotes the formula and one encounter gives it as instruction to a ruler.
No emptiness to fall into is the National Teacher's answer when pressed whether no-mind collapses into blankness: if emptiness itself is absent, there is nowhere for a fall to stand.
To strike ice seeking fire is to use means incapable of producing the sought result; masters apply it to conceptual explanation, strained case handling, and the effort abandoned at breakthrough.
